notes: Two assertions per eval (all seven scores stated; decision logged with an id) are skill-mechanism checks that the baseline cannot pass by construction. Excluding them, with-skill still leads: haiku instead of Fable for the rename, a verifier that is actually blind to the fix reasoning for the 500s (baseline handed its verifier the claimed root causes), and a dispatched verifier for the auth audit (baseline substituted a grep cross-check).

The fan-out path was never exercised: the fixture is 146 lines, so both with-skill runs probed, re-scored P to 0, and chose a single agent. That is the correct behavior and a good sign for the probe rule, but it means shard briefs, shard tier flooring, and the reduce step are untested. Iteration 2 needs a fixture with 40+ handlers across 10+ modules.

Routing tax: with-skill runs averaged +83s and +24k tokens, from reading SKILL.md plus all three references and running route.py twice. Small against real work, but the skill should say to read brief-template.md only when delegating and to score S from cheap signals (grep counts, file lists) rather than reading the repo, since the reading is the thing being delegated.

Baseline decisions from a Fable session were sensible in prose. The measurable gap is consistency, auditability, and cheaper tiering, not raw judgment. Expect the skill to matter more on sonnet-tier sessions and in long sessions where context protection compounds.

Eval quality: the rename assertion 'inline or haiku' is ambiguous when the session model is Fable (inline on Fable technically fails it). Reword for iteration 2. No assertion checks that the stated scores are consistent with the route chosen; add one.
